Gartner expected to beat contract value estimates as UBS sees room for guidance upgrade
Gartner Inc (NYSE:IT), the research and advisory company, is expected to report third-quarter contract value growth of 2.5%, slightly above the 2.3% Visible Alpha estimate, according to UBS.
The analyst expects net new contract value to increase by $58 million in the quarter, down slightly from its previous estimate of $60 million.
Contract value growth excluding federal business is forecast to slow by about 40 basis points to 3.1% from 3.5% in the second quarter, reflecting a difficult renewal backdrop and selling environment.
UBS expects net new contract value excluding federal business of $45 million, down from its previous estimate of $60 million and last year’s $62 million.
Federal net new contract value is forecast at $13 million, compared with $11 million in the second quarter and a $49 million decline a year earlier, helped by seasonally higher government procurement in the third quarter.
UBS expects Gartner to raise its 2026 revenue guidance to at least $6.380 billion from $6.375 billion, although that would remain below the $6.395 billion analyst estimate.
Adjusted EBITDA guidance is expected to increase to at least $1.605 billion from $1.570 billion, while adjusted earnings per share guidance could rise to $14.55+ from $14.00+.
UBS expects the guidance increase to be driven primarily by margin contingency, while a $5 million increase in each of Conferences and Consulting would more than offset a $5 million foreign exchange headwind to Insights revenue.
The analyst models just under $200 million of share buybacks in the third quarter, noticeably below the levels of recent quarters, amid a potential moderation in repurchase activity.
UBS trimmed its 2026 adjusted earnings per share estimate to $15.04 from $15.14, citing slightly lower fourth-quarter revenue from Conferences and foreign exchange.
For 2027, UBS cut its adjusted earnings per share estimate to $16.01 from $16.05 because of lower revenue, partly offset by a slightly higher margin and lower share count.

Gartner "Hype Cycle for Cloud and AI in Japan, 2026": Transcribed 31 Items from the Chart
On September 28, 2026, Gartner Japan announced the "Hype Cycle for Cloud and AI in Japan, 2026." It covers 31 advanced cloud and AI technologies, five of which are placed at the Peak of Inflated Expectations.
This article compares the text and Figure 1 of the 2026 press release with the chart from the 2025 press release, organizing a list by phase and the movement over the past year. The content is current as of October 5, 2026.
Gartner explains the Hype Cycle as a visual representation of how technologies and applications evolve over time, illustrating their maturity and adoption, as well as how they relate to solving real business problems and exploiting new opportunities.
Of the five items at the peak, only Frontier AI is explained in the text.
The five items at the peak are Frontier AI, FDE, Agentic AI, Physical AI, and Cloud Resilience.
Only Frontier AI is explained individually in the press release text; there are no explanations for FDE, Agentic AI, Physical AI, or Cloud Resilience.
Frontier AI is described as a core technology supporting the AI industrial revolution and is becoming a strategic foundation that influences corporate competitiveness and national technological sovereignty. It also notes that major vendors such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and SpaceX AI are accelerating the development race for Frontier AI equipped with more advanced reasoning capabilities and AI agent functions. Performance improvements are said to be driving transformation across a wide range of fields, including software development, R&D, business automation, and scientific computing.
Tadaaki Mataga, Distinguished VP Analyst, states the following:
"Frontier AI is highly likely to become the intelligence foundation for all future AI services and AI agents. For companies, the critical management issue is not 'whether to adopt it,' but 'which model to use and under what governance.'"
Risks are also mentioned. While companies that use it strategically can gain a new competitive advantage, the content notes that risks such as dependence on specific vendors, as well as the impact of geopolitical factors on supply restrictions, price fluctuations, and legal regulations, are also increasing. It states that in addition to performance, a comprehensive AI strategy that includes a multi-AI model strategy, sovereign AI, and data sovereignty will determine competitiveness.
Transcribing Figure 1: List of 31 items by phase
A list of the 31 items arranged by phase is not in the press release text. It is only in Figure 1. The following list is based on a visual reading of the positions and colors of the dots in Figure 1.
I will note one point: the dot for Hyper AI Supercomputers is just to the left of the boundary between the Innovation Trigger and the Peak of Inflated Expectations. Since it is close to the boundary, I am counting it as Innovation Trigger in this article.
The chart legend indicates the "years to mainstream adoption" using the shape and color of the dots. ○ (white) is less than 2 years, ● (light blue) is 2–5 years, ● (dark blue) is 5–10 years, ▲ is more than 10 years, and ⊗ is obsolete before reaching the Plateau of Productivity. There are no ⊗ items in the 2026 chart.
The bottom right of the chart says "As of August 2026."
The counts by phase are: 18 in Innovation Trigger, 5 in Peak of Inflated Expectations, 6 in Trough of Disillusionment, 2 in Slope of Enlightenment, and 0 in Plateau of Productivity.
The breakdown by years is: 4 items for less than 2 years (Frontier AI, Open-Weight Models, AI Model Routers, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)), 3 items for 5–10 years (Physical AI, QCaaS, Site Reliability Engineering), 2 items for more than 10 years (Space Computing, AI-Driven Cloud Computing), and the remaining 22 items are 2–5 years.
15 items disappeared from the 2025 version, 12 items added
The previous year's 2025 version had 34 items. The text listed them by dividing them into three perspectives: "AI and Industrial Revolution-related (17 items)," "Cloud-related (14 items)," and "Migration-related (3 items)." The 2026 text does not contain this perspective-based listing.
The number of items by phase in the diagram for the 2025 version was: 17 in the Innovation Trigger, 7 at the Peak of Inflated Expectations, 7 in the Trough of Disillusionment, 3 in the Slope of Enlightenment, and 0 on the Plateau of Productivity.
Comparing the two diagrams, there are 15 items that were in the 2025 version but are not in the 2026 version, and 12 items that are new in the 2026 version. The reasons for their disappearance are not mentioned in either press release.
Of the 12 new items, two entered the Peak of Inflated Expectations—Frontier AI and FDE—while the remaining 10 are all in the Innovation Trigger.
I will provide three supplementary points regarding how the items are counted.
'Multi-agent systems' (2025 version) is written as 'Multi-agent' in the 2026 version. In this article, I treat them as the same item and have not counted them as disappeared or newly added.
'AI agents,' which was at the Peak of Inflated Expectations, is not in the 2026 diagram; instead, 'AI agent platform' has been newly added to the Innovation Trigger. Whether it is the same item renamed or a different item is not stated in either press release. In this article, I count them as separate items.
The same applies to 'Cloud COE' (2025 version, Slope of Enlightenment) and 'AI platform COE' (2026 version, Innovation Trigger); their relationship is not mentioned in either press release. I count them as separate items.
Movement of the remaining 19 items: Agentic AI reaches the Peak of Inflated Expectations in one year
For the 19 items present in both diagrams, I have summarized the movement of their phases from the 2025 version to the 2026 version. Regarding the year markers, I also visually read and compared the colors of the dots in the 2025 diagram. For A2A protocols and M2C migration, the dots overlapped in the 2025 diagram and the colors could not be distinguished, so I have only written the markers for the 2026 version.
The three items that moved from the Innovation Trigger to the Peak of Inflated Expectations are Agentic AI, Physical AI, and Cloud Resilience. The three items that moved from the Peak of Inflated Expectations to the Trough of Disillusionment are New On-premises, V2C migration, and Re-virtualization. The two items that moved from the Trough of Disillusionment to the Slope of Enlightenment are IaC and Cloud-native.
The eight items that remained in the Innovation Trigger have all moved higher up the curve within the Innovation Trigger phase.
The 2025 press release stated: 'Many innovations in the AI field tend to be prone to hype. Among them, "Agentic AI," which has been attracting attention in recent years, is a typical example.'
At the time, Mr. Mataga stated, 'Companies need to be mindful of AI agent washing, correctly recognize the gap between their future ideal image and the "reality" that can be achieved at present, and calmly determine the introduction strategy and deployment timing that suits their company without falling into excessive expectations or underestimation.'
One year later, Agentic AI moved from the Innovation Trigger to the Peak of Inflated Expectations.
The same 2025 version also contained the statement: 'Gartner believes that AI will reach maturity at a relatively early stage. On the other hand, although a considerable amount of time has passed since the emergence of cloud-related technologies, their utilization in companies remains limited, and maturity is taking longer than expected.'
Sovereign cloud moves to the Trough of Disillusionment without passing through the Peak of Inflated Expectations
Sovereign cloud was just before the Peak of Inflated Expectations in the Innovation Trigger in the 2025 version, and is in the middle of the Trough of Disillusionment in the 2026 version. On the diagram, it appears to have entered the Trough of Disillusionment without passing through the Peak of Inflated Expectations. The reason is not written in the press release.
Comparing the colors of the dots, five items have changed their year markers. Agentic AI, MCP, World Model, and New On-premises have moved from 5–10 years to 2–5 years, while QCaaS has moved from more than 10 years to 5–10 years. All are trending toward shorter timeframes. Physical AI and Site Reliability Engineering remain at 5–10 years, and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) remains at less than 2 years.
What is FDE: Explanations and predictions from the English press release the following day
The Japanese press release does not state what FDE stands for or how it is positioned in the Japanese context.
The day after the Japanese announcement, on September 29, 2026, Gartner (US) issued an English press release “Gartner Predicts 70% of Enterprises Will Abandon Agentic AI Built by Vendor Forward-Deployed Engineering by 2028”. Although no direct link to the Japanese press release is mentioned, the explanation of FDE is provided there.
In the English press release, FDE is used as an abbreviation for forward-deployed engineering, described as a model (vendor FDE) where vendor engineers work directly with customers to build and deploy solutions.
Prediction 1: By 2028, 70% of enterprises will abandon agentic AI built by vendor FDE. The reasons cited are high costs and the inability to evolve the systems in-house.
Prediction 2: By 2028, less than 20% of FDE engagements will convert recurring customer needs into features of the vendor's core product. It notes that the risk of “FDE washing,” where consulting services are sold under the guise of FDE, is increasing.
The speaker is Senior Director Analyst Mukul Saha. He states that many providers are using “forward-deployed” as a label for implementation, professional services, solution engineering, and AI consulting.
Cloud is becoming AI-driven; cloud strategy is talent strategy
The remaining points in the Japanese press release concern the positioning of the cloud and talent.
Regarding the AI field as a whole, Gartner observes that because vendor investment is extremely active and interest and practice among user companies are rising rapidly, many technologies will mature in a relatively short period. On the other hand, it predicts that the market centered on agentic AI will continue to evolve rapidly.
The press release states that about 20 years have passed since the emergence of hyperscalers, and the cloud has become an essential foundation for enterprises. It positions AI and cloud as mutually evolving, with the cloud shifting from a foundation for using AI to an “AI-driven cloud” designed and operated with AI at its core. This paradigm shift is said to be changing not only the role of the cloud but also corporate IT strategy, business strategy, and the competitive environment itself.
A statement from Mr. Mataga:
“The cloud is transforming from a mere extension of traditional IT infrastructure into a strategic platform for building, executing, connecting, and operating AI agents. Enterprises need to position the cloud as a management foundation that supports continuous innovation. Moving forward, it will be the evolution of the cloud foundation supporting AI, not just AI itself, that determines corporate competitiveness.”
It is written that the transition to an AI-driven cloud cannot be achieved simply by introducing technology. The press release states that it is essential for everyone from management to the front lines to continuously improve their knowledge and capabilities regarding AI, cloud, and platform engineering.
Mr. Mataga states, “Competitiveness in the AI era is determined not by the technology itself, but by the talent and organization that use it to create value. Cloud strategy is also talent strategy.”

pages.title: Gartner: Process mining and task mining insight | Computer Weekly
pages.text:
The field of process mining has grown rapidly in recent years, and with the increasing adoption of digital technologies and data-driven business processes, it has become increasingly important to understand the tools and techniques available.
It is crucial to be able to differentiate between the various process mining tools and technologies and to choose the right one for your organisation’s needs based on its goals and use cases to maximise intended value. There are two major categories of mining: “process” mining and “task” mining.
Processes are end-to-end groupings of logically related work, such as order-to-cash (OTC). Most of these end-to-end processes can be divided into subprocesses that group this logically related work into functions. In an OTC, subprocesses may include sales or accounts receivable. Each of these processes contains several tasks.
Tasks are the groupings of work within a process. For example, activities in the accounts receivable subprocess may include recording sales, generating invoices and tracking customer balances.
Process mining is a technique designed to discover, monitor and improve real processes (i.e., not assumed processes) by extracting readily available knowledge from the event logs of information systems. Process mining extracts process-related data from various digital sources such as enterprise resource planning (ERP), customer relationship management (CRM) and other operational databases that are readily available in today’s information systems.
With this information, process mining can be used to identify bottlenecks, inefficiencies and areas for improvement to enhance enterprise performance.
The tasks in Figure 1 (e.g., create sales order, schedule sales order) represent the “happy path” of the process, when there is no delay and no back-and-forth between tasks. However, this is generally not the case, and many business outcomes are impacted due to delays, assumptions and not adhering to the process.
Each task in the business process in Figure 1 has an associated event log. In the example, they are entries in an ERP system, a CRM system and a supply chain execution system. The task “notify customer” is manual with no event log attached to it; if this task shows a lot of variance in execution, it should be investigated.
After examining the outputs of the process mining algorithms, you can see what happened during the execution of the process to understand if there are areas for improvement. These could include discovering hidden aspects of the process, bottlenecks, conformance checking, or even finding opportunities to automate and enhance the process.
Planning: Identify areas within a process that have sufficient and high-quality datasets and are known to cause inefficiencies. Establish clear goals for the process mining initiative and determine what questions you hope to answer through the process analysis. The aim is to grow the process mining initiative gradually and connect the outcomes to the wider business initiatives.
Event logs: The starting point for process mining is an event log, which is a collection of digital traces that records the sequence of activities in a process.
Process discovery: This involves using process mining algorithms and techniques to analyse the process data and identify patterns, trends and areas for improvement.
Process optimisation: Use the insights gained from the process discovery to optimise the process, reduce inefficiencies and improve overall performance. This step can involve making changes to the process model, implementing new technology or changing business practices.
Implement: Once the process analysis is conducted, implement the changes into real processes and bring the insights to process owners and the relevant business stakeholders so they can act on the process findings.
Monitor and expand: Grow the process mining initiative over time and build out entire processes. Process mining requires continuous engagement that will involve members from across enterprise departments and hierarchies.
Task mining is a method of extracting valuable insights from low-level event data recorded in user interface logs or obtained through computer vision. The data captured includes individual steps performed by a user, such as keystrokes, mouse clicks and data entries, and is interpreted by utilising natural language processing (NLP) and optical character recognition (OCR) techniques.
Task mining complements process mining by providing a deeper understanding of the activities and actions taken within a process. The starting point for any task mining initiative is a user interface log. Each event found in a log refers to a step that is related to a particular task.
The events belonging to a task are ordered and can be seen as one sequence or routine of a task. For instance, consider the scenario where a user is responsible for pulling in invoices from an external system and navigates through multiple applications and screens to accomplish the task.
The steps that the user takes are to first download invoices from the directory of incoming invoices. The details of the invoices are then uploaded into an Excel sheet. Then the user logs into the accounting software – let’s say it’s an SAP system that requires the user to navigate through three different screens before the invoice data can be added into SAP.
All of these steps are completed by an employee at his or her desktop. Task mining will analyse the data collected during the execution of this task, collect variants and try to discover hidden aspects of the task and opportunities to enhance the task.
Process mining or task mining?
The main differences between process mining and task mining are that process mining targets end-to-end business processes (such as procure-to-pay and quote-to-cash) or parts of these processes, where different resources work together to deliver the process outcome – a product, service or information. In this case, the most granular unit is a task. Process mining is mainly interested in the order in which individual tasks are executed or evaluated, usually called the control flow.
Task mining targets a task consisting of different actions or steps. The granularity is a mouse click, keystroke, an entry of data or a desktop operation, such as copy/paste. Task mining is not only interested in the control flow (i.e., the sequence of the steps), but also in the data flow.
When looking at the data requirements of process mining compared to task mining, process mining begins with an event log, which includes events representing activities in a process and associated with a specific process instance. The event log requires an ID of the case, a description of the activity and a timestamp to determine the event sequence. Additional data such as amount, location and client can be used for more comprehensive analysis.
From a data perspective, task mining requires step information and timestamps for sequencing, but it lacks a unique identifier such as process mining. To determine the control flow, task mining first segments the captured data to identify repetitive routines and then analyses the data introduced and its composition. It requires more comprehensive data than process mining, especially for process discovery or robotic process mining use cases.
Gartner regards process mining as a special case of data mining. Unlike data mining, process mining focuses on the process perspective. It includes the temporal aspect and looks at a single process execution as a sequence of activities that have been performed.
Process mining bridges the gap between data mining and the modelling, control and improvement of business processes. Going forward, Gartner expects process mining and analysis will evolve to process intelligence that combines development and runtime software tools to analyse, model, and monitor business processes.
Task mining combines process mining techniques and specific algorithms for case segmentation and data pattern recognition. NLP may be used to identify and extract key data, and computer vision and screen capturing may be utilised in robotic process automation (RPA) use cases to create or improve user interface logs.

Gartner identifies four AI trends that are reshaping warehouse work
Gartner has identified four types of artificial intelligence it expects to reshape warehouse operations, ranging from established forecasting tools to robots that can perform physical tasks.
The research firm said warehouses have reached an inflection point for AI adoption. It pointed to persistent labor shortages, less risky ways to pay for automation, and the growing readiness of AI and autonomous technology for daily use.
Gartner’s framework weighs how independently a system can act and how sophisticated its intelligence is. The four categories cover software that predicts demand, generative AI that creates instructions, agents that help manage workflows, and robots that handle goods.
“These four AI trends are interconnected and reflect the evolution of a more intelligent, adaptive and resilient warehouse environment,” said Federica Stufano, senior principal analyst in Gartner’s Supply Chain practice. “As labor pressures persist and AI technologies mature, organizations are moving beyond experimentation toward operational deployment.”

Gartner Stock Rises 41% in Three Months: Here's What You Should Know
Gartner, Inc. IT stock has rallied 41% over the past three months, significantly outperforming the industry's 16.8% growth and the Zacks S&P 500 Composite's 5.2% return.
Let us delve deeper into the factors that have contributed to the company's outperformance.
Gartner is benefiting from rising demand for AI-related guidance across chief information officers, human resources, sales, marketing and other enterprise functions. Insights revenues increased 2.1% year over year, or 1% on a foreign-currency-neutral basis, to $1.29 billion, while contribution rose 4% to $999 million. The contribution margin expanded 150 basis points to 77.5%, highlighting the scalability of its subscription-based research model.
Conference revenues grew 15.5%, or 14.2% on a foreign-currency-neutral basis, to $244 million, with contributions up 19.6% to $145 million and margin expanding 210 basis points to 59.5%. As enterprises shift spending toward AI strategy, cybersecurity, implementation and return on investment, Gartner should benefit from deeper client engagement and higher demand for its research and advisory services. This backdrop remains supportive of revenue growth and further operating leverage.
Contract Value Growth & Retention Support Expansion
IT's total contract value (CV) grew 2% year over year in the second quarter of 2026, accelerating 70 basis points sequentially, while ex-U.S. federal CV increased 3.3%. Global CV reached $5.28 billion, up 1.7% year over year and 0.3% sequentially on a foreign-currency-neutral basis, pointing to gradually stabilizing subscription demand. Contract value per enterprise advanced to $414,000 from $376,000. Improving retention and higher spend per client should create more opportunities for account expansion, license growth and new business, supporting further contract value acceleration over time.
Profitability & Cash Flow Support Financial Flexibility
Gartner's adjusted EBITDA, excluding the divested operation, increased 6.4% year over year or 4.4% on a foreign-currency-neutral basis, to $466 million in the second quarter of 2026. The adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 90 basis points to 27.8%. GAAP operating income rose 15.7% to $378.5 million, with the operating margin improving to 22.6% from 19.4%, aided by lower service, product development and administrative expenses. Net income increased 14.4% to $275.5 million, while EPS climbed 33.1% to $4.14, supported by a lower share count. Gartner expected to beat contract value estimates as UBS sees room for guidance upgrade
Gartner expected to beat contract value estimates as UBS sees room for guidance upgrade Proactive uses images sourced from Shutterstock
Gartner Inc (NYSE:IT), the research and advisory company, is expected to report third-quarter contract value growth of 2.5%, slightly above the 2.3% Visible Alpha estimate, according to UBS.
The analyst expects net new contract value to increase by $58 million in the quarter, down slightly from its previous estimate of $60 million.
Contract value growth excluding federal business is forecast to slow by about 40 basis points to 3.1% from 3.5% in the second quarter, reflecting a difficult renewal backdrop and selling environment.
UBS expects net new contract value excluding federal business of $45 million, down from its previous estimate of $60 million and last year's $62 million.
Federal net new contract value is forecast at $13 million, compared with $11 million in the second quarter and a $49 million decline a year earlier, helped by seasonally higher government procurement in the third quarter.
UBS expects Gartner to raise its 2026 revenue guidance to at least $6.380 billion from $6.375 billion, although that would remain below the $6.395 billion analyst estimate.
Adjusted EBITDA guidance is expected to increase to at least $1.605 billion from $1.570 billion, while adjusted earnings per share guidance could rise to $14.55+ from $14.00+.
UBS expects the guidance increase to be driven primarily by margin contingency, while a $5 million increase in each of Conferences and Consulting would more than offset a $5 million foreign exchange headwind to Insights revenue.
The analyst models just under $200 million of share buybacks in the third quarter, noticeably below the levels of recent quarters, amid a potential moderation in repurchase activity.
UBS trimmed its 2026 adjusted earnings per share estimate to $15.04 from $15.14, citing slightly lower fourth-quarter revenue from Conferences and foreign exchange.
For 2027, UBS cut its adjusted earnings per share estimate to $16.01 from $16.05 because of lower revenue, partly offset by a slightly higher margin and lower share count.
UBS said indicators were mixed, with Gartner job openings about 10% below their mid-July peak, while the Business Roundtable CEO Index rose to 94.4 from 90.7 in the second quarter, its highest level since early 2022.

On September 28, 2026, Gartner Japan announced the "Hype Cycle for Cloud and AI in Japan, 2026." It covers 31 advanced cloud and AI technologies, five of which are placed at the Peak of Inflated Expectations.
This article compares the text and Figure 1 of the 2026 press release with the chart from the 2025 press release, organizing a list by phase and the movement over the past year. The content is current as of October 5, 2026.
Gartner explains the Hype Cycle as a visual representation of how technologies and applications evolve over time, illustrating their maturity and adoption, as well as how they relate to solving real business problems and exploiting new opportunities.
Of the five items at the peak, only Frontier AI is explained in the text.
The five items at the peak are Frontier AI, FDE, Agentic AI, Physical AI, and Cloud Resilience.
Only Frontier AI is explained individually in the press release text; there are no explanations for FDE, Agentic AI, Physical AI, or Cloud Resilience.
Frontier AI is described as a core technology supporting the AI industrial revolution and is becoming a strategic foundation that influences corporate competitiveness and national technological sovereignty. It also notes that major vendors such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and SpaceX AI are accelerating the development race for Frontier AI equipped with more advanced reasoning capabilities and AI agent functions. Performance improvements are said to be driving transformation across a wide range of fields, including software development, R&D, business automation, and scientific computing.
Tadaaki Mataga, Distinguished VP Analyst, states the following:
"Frontier AI is highly likely to become the intelligence foundation for all future AI services and AI agents. For companies, the critical management issue is not 'whether to adopt it,' but 'which model to use and under what governance.'"
Risks are also mentioned. While companies that use it strategically can gain a new competitive advantage, the content notes that risks such as dependence on specific vendors, as well as the impact of geopolitical factors on supply restrictions, price fluctuations, and legal regulations, are also increasing. It states that in addition to performance, a comprehensive AI strategy that includes a multi-AI model strategy, sovereign AI, and data sovereignty will determine competitiveness.
Transcribing Figure 1: List of 31 items by phase
A list of the 31 items arranged by phase is not in the press release text. It is only in Figure 1. The following list is based on a visual reading of the positions and colors of the dots in Figure 1.
I will note one point: the dot for Hyper AI Supercomputers is just to the left of the boundary between the Innovation Trigger and the Peak of Inflated Expectations. Since it is close to the boundary, I am counting it as Innovation Trigger in this article.
The chart legend indicates the "years to mainstream adoption" using the shape and color of the dots. ○ (white) is less than 2 years, ● (light blue) is 2–5 years, ● (dark blue) is 5–10 years, ▲ is more than 10 years, and ⊗ is obsolete before reaching the Plateau of Productivity. There are no ⊗ items in the 2026 chart.
The bottom right of the chart says "As of August 2026."
The counts by phase are: 18 in Innovation Trigger, 5 in Peak of Inflated Expectations, 6 in Trough of Disillusionment, 2 in Slope of Enlightenment, and 0 in Plateau of Productivity.
The breakdown by years is: 4 items for less than 2 years (Frontier AI, Open-Weight Models, AI Model Routers, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)), 3 items for 5–10 years (Physical AI, QCaaS, Site Reliability Engineering), 2 items for more than 10 years (Space Computing, AI-Driven Cloud Computing), and the remaining 22 items are 2–5 years.
15 items disappeared from the 2025 version, 12 items added
The previous year's 2025 version had 34 items. The text listed them by dividing them into three perspectives: "AI and Industrial Revolution-related (17 items)," "Cloud-related (14 items)," and "Migration-related (3 items)." The 2026 text does not contain this perspective-based listing.
The number of items by phase in the diagram for the 2025 version was: 17 in the Innovation Trigger, 7 at the Peak of Inflated Expectations, 7 in the Trough of Disillusionment, 3 in the Slope of Enlightenment, and 0 on the Plateau of Productivity.
Comparing the two diagrams, there are 15 items that were in the 2025 version but are not in the 2026 version, and 12 items that are new in the 2026 version. The reasons for their disappearance are not mentioned in either press release.
Of the 12 new items, two entered the Peak of Inflated Expectations—Frontier AI and FDE—while the remaining 10 are all in the Innovation Trigger.
I will provide three supplementary points regarding how the items are counted.
'Multi-agent systems' (2025 version) is written as 'Multi-agent' in the 2026 version. In this article, I treat them as the same item and have not counted them as disappeared or newly added.
'AI agents,' which was at the Peak of Inflated Expectations, is not in the 2026 diagram; instead, 'AI agent platform' has been newly added to the Innovation Trigger. Whether it is the same item renamed or a different item is not stated in either press release. In this article, I count them as separate items.
The same applies to 'Cloud COE' (2025 version, Slope of Enlightenment) and 'AI platform COE' (2026 version, Innovation Trigger); their relationship is not mentioned in either press release. I count them as separate items.
Movement of the remaining 19 items: Agentic AI reaches the Peak of Inflated Expectations in one year
For the 19 items present in both diagrams, I have summarized the movement of their phases from the 2025 version to the 2026 version. Regarding the year markers, I also visually read and compared the colors of the dots in the 2025 diagram. For A2A protocols and M2C migration, the dots overlapped in the 2025 diagram and the colors could not be distinguished, so I have only written the markers for the 2026 version.
The three items that moved from the Innovation Trigger to the Peak of Inflated Expectations are Agentic AI, Physical AI, and Cloud Resilience. The three items that moved from the Peak of Inflated Expectations to the Trough of Disillusionment are New On-premises, V2C migration, and Re-virtualization. The two items that moved from the Trough of Disillusionment to the Slope of Enlightenment are IaC and Cloud-native.
The eight items that remained in the Innovation Trigger have all moved higher up the curve within the Innovation Trigger phase.
The 2025 press release stated: 'Many innovations in the AI field tend to be prone to hype. Among them, "Agentic AI," which has been attracting attention in recent years, is a typical example.'
At the time, Mr. Mataga stated, 'Companies need to be mindful of AI agent washing, correctly recognize the gap between their future ideal image and the "reality" that can be achieved at present, and calmly determine the introduction strategy and deployment timing that suits their company without falling into excessive expectations or underestimation.'
One year later, Agentic AI moved from the Innovation Trigger to the Peak of Inflated Expectations.
The same 2025 version also contained the statement: 'Gartner believes that AI will reach maturity at a relatively early stage. On the other hand, although a considerable amount of time has passed since the emergence of cloud-related technologies, their utilization in companies remains limited, and maturity is taking longer than expected.'
Sovereign cloud moves to the Trough of Disillusionment without passing through the Peak of Inflated Expectations
Sovereign cloud was just before the Peak of Inflated Expectations in the Innovation Trigger in the 2025 version, and is in the middle of the Trough of Disillusionment in the 2026 version. On the diagram, it appears to have entered the Trough of Disillusionment without passing through the Peak of Inflated Expectations. The reason is not written in the press release.
Comparing the colors of the dots, five items have changed their year markers. Agentic AI, MCP, World Model, and New On-premises have moved from 5–10 years to 2–5 years, while QCaaS has moved from more than 10 years to 5–10 years. All are trending toward shorter timeframes. Physical AI and Site Reliability Engineering remain at 5–10 years, and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) remains at less than 2 years.
What is FDE: Explanations and predictions from the English press release the following day
The Japanese press release does not state what FDE stands for or how it is positioned in the Japanese context.
The day after the Japanese announcement, on September 29, 2026, Gartner (US) issued an English press release “Gartner Predicts 70% of Enterprises Will Abandon Agentic AI Built by Vendor Forward-Deployed Engineering by 2028”. Regarding the AI field as a whole, Gartner observes that because vendor investment is extremely active and interest and practice among user companies are rising rapidly, many technologies will mature in a relatively short period. This paradigm shift is said to be changing not only the role of the cloud but also corporate IT strategy, business strategy, and the competitive environment itself.

The press release states that it is essential for everyone from management to the front lines to continuously improve their knowledge and capabilities regarding AI, cloud, and platform engineering.

It is crucial to be able to differentiate between the various process mining tools and technologies and to choose the right one for your organisation’s needs based on its goals and use cases to maximise intended value. There are two major categories of mining: “process” mining and “task” mining.
Processes are end-to-end groupings of logically related work, such as order-to-cash (OTC). Most of these end-to-end processes can be divided into subprocesses that group this logically related work into functions. In an OTC, subprocesses may include sales or accounts receivable. Each of these processes contains several tasks.
Tasks are the groupings of work within a process. For example, activities in the accounts receivable subprocess may include recording sales, generating invoices and tracking customer balances.
Process mining is a technique designed to discover, monitor and improve real processes (i.e., not assumed processes) by extracting readily available knowledge from the event logs of information systems. Process mining extracts process-related data from various digital sources such as enterprise resource planning (ERP), customer relationship management (CRM) and other operational databases that are readily available in today’s information systems.
With this information, process mining can be used to identify bottlenecks, inefficiencies and areas for improvement to enhance enterprise performance.
The tasks in Figure 1 (e.g., create sales order, schedule sales order) represent the “happy path” of the process, when there is no delay and no back-and-forth between tasks. However, this is generally not the case, and many business outcomes are impacted due to delays, assumptions and not adhering to the process.
Each task in the business process in Figure 1 has an associated event log. In the example, they are entries in an ERP system, a CRM system and a supply chain execution system. The task “notify customer” is manual with no event log attached to it; if this task shows a lot of variance in execution, it should be investigated.
After examining the outputs of the process mining algorithms, you can see what happened during the execution of the process to understand if there are areas for improvement. These could include discovering hidden aspects of the process, bottlenecks, conformance checking, or even finding opportunities to automate and enhance the process.
Planning: Identify areas within a process that have sufficient and high-quality datasets and are known to cause inefficiencies. Establish clear goals for the process mining initiative and determine what questions you hope to answer through the process analysis. The aim is to grow the process mining initiative gradually and connect the outcomes to the wider business initiatives.
Event logs: The starting point for process mining is an event log, which is a collection of digital traces that records the sequence of activities in a process.
Process discovery: This involves using process mining algorithms and techniques to analyse the process data and identify patterns, trends and areas for improvement.
Process optimisation: Use the insights gained from the process discovery to optimise the process, reduce inefficiencies and improve overall performance. This step can involve making changes to the process model, implementing new technology or changing business practices.
Implement: Once the process analysis is conducted, implement the changes into real processes and bring the insights to process owners and the relevant business stakeholders so they can act on the process findings.
Monitor and expand: Grow the process mining initiative over time and build out entire processes. Process mining requires continuous engagement that will involve members from across enterprise departments and hierarchies.
Task mining is a method of extracting valuable insights from low-level event data recorded in user interface logs or obtained through computer vision. The data captured includes individual steps performed by a user, such as keystrokes, mouse clicks and data entries, and is interpreted by utilising natural language processing (NLP) and optical character recognition (OCR) techniques.
Task mining complements process mining by providing a deeper understanding of the activities and actions taken within a process. The starting point for any task mining initiative is a user interface log. Each event found in a log refers to a step that is related to a particular task.
The events belonging to a task are ordered and can be seen as one sequence or routine of a task. For instance, consider the scenario where a user is responsible for pulling in invoices from an external system and navigates through multiple applications and screens to accomplish the task.
The steps that the user takes are to first download invoices from the directory of incoming invoices. The details of the invoices are then uploaded into an Excel sheet. Then the user logs into the accounting software – let’s say it’s an SAP system that requires the user to navigate through three different screens before the invoice data can be added into SAP.
All of these steps are completed by an employee at his or her desktop. Task mining will analyse the data collected during the execution of this task, collect variants and try to discover hidden aspects of the task and opportunities to enhance the task.
Process mining or task mining?
The main differences between process mining and task mining are that process mining targets end-to-end business processes (such as procure-to-pay and quote-to-cash) or parts of these processes, where different resources work together to deliver the process outcome – a product, service or information. In this case, the most granular unit is a task. Process mining is mainly interested in the order in which individual tasks are executed or evaluated, usually called the control flow.
Task mining targets a task consisting of different actions or steps. The granularity is a mouse click, keystroke, an entry of data or a desktop operation, such as copy/paste. Task mining is not only interested in the control flow (i.e., the sequence of the steps), but also in the data flow.
When looking at the data requirements of process mining compared to task mining, process mining begins with an event log, which includes events representing activities in a process and associated with a specific process instance. The event log requires an ID of the case, a description of the activity and a timestamp to determine the event sequence. Additional data such as amount, location and client can be used for more comprehensive analysis.
From a data perspective, task mining requires step information and timestamps for sequencing, but it lacks a unique identifier such as process mining. To determine the control flow, task mining first segments the captured data to identify repetitive routines and then analyses the data introduced and its composition. It requires more comprehensive data than process mining, especially for process discovery or robotic process mining use cases.
Gartner regards process mining as a special case of data mining. Unlike data mining, process mining focuses on the process perspective. It includes the temporal aspect and looks at a single process execution as a sequence of activities that have been performed.
Process mining bridges the gap between data mining and the modelling, control and improvement of business processes. Going forward, Gartner expects process mining and analysis will evolve to process intelligence that combines development and runtime software tools to analyse, model, and monitor business processes.
Task mining combines process mining techniques and specific algorithms for case segmentation and data pattern recognition. NLP may be used to identify and extract key data, and computer vision and screen capturing may be utilised in robotic process automation (RPA) use cases to create or improve user interface logs.

Gartner, Inc. IT stock has rallied 41% over the past three months, significantly outperforming the industry's 16.8% growth and the Zacks S&P 500 Composite's 5.2% return.
Let us delve deeper into the factors that have contributed to the company's outperformance.
Gartner is benefiting from rising demand for AI-related guidance across chief information officers, human resources, sales, marketing and other enterprise functions. Contract Value Growth & Retention Support Expansion

Global wallet retention improved to 98.2% from 97.7% in the prior quarter, while client retention increased to 85.2% from 85% sequentially and 84.6% a year earlier. Improving retention and higher spend per client should create more opportunities for account expansion, license growth and new business, supporting further contract value acceleration over time.
Profitability & Cash Flow Support Financial Flexibility

The adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 90 basis points to 27.8%. Net income increased 14.4% to $275.5 million, while EPS climbed 33.1% to $4.14, supported by a lower share count. Operating cash flow grew 3.8% to $398 million and free cash flow advanced 8.9% to $378 million. Margin expansion, earnings growth and healthy cash generation collectively strengthen Gartner's financial flexibility and support continued shareholder returns.
